claims.text: The target material is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent element.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has inherent compositional disorder.
A multiscale framework combining DFT-derived interatomic force constants with classical molecular dynamics can predict phonon thermal conductivity in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Supercells larger than 10 nm will be used in the molecular-dynamics simulations.
Chemical disorder in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produces local lattice distortions and atomic-level randomness.
Local lattice distortions influence interatomic forces in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder enhance phonon-defect scattering.
Explicitly modeling local distortions and their effects on interatomic forces will capture disorder-induced phonon-defect scattering more accurately.
Conventional averaging methods overlook phonon-defect scattering associated with local lattice distortions.
Explicit treatment of disorder-induced scattering will improve the accuracy of predicted phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed framework will reduce predictive error by approximately 20–25% relative to conventional methods.
The framework's predicted phonon thermal conductivity will closely correlate with experimental measurements.
The proposed approach is applicable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi between 300 K and 700 K.
Application to other alloy systems or temperatures outside 300–700 K may require further calibration.
Finite supercell sizes may fail to capture long-range disorder effects and thereby reduce predictive accuracy.
The framework is falsified if its error reduction relative to the conventional model is less than 20%.
The framework is falsified if its predictions deviate by more than 30% from experimental measurements.
